property_summary: For any caller and any value v >= MinDeposit, calling Deposit with value v increases that caller's balances by v (i.e., balances(caller) after Deposit equals prior + v); the mutant that changes >= to > breaks this by rejecting deposits exactly equal to MinDeposit so balances do not increase for v == MinDeposit.

For any caller and any deposit amount >= MinDeposit, calling Deposit results in balances(caller) increasing by that amount; the mutant changing >= to > rejects deposits equal to MinDeposit, so for amount == MinDeposit the balance does not increase.

For any depositor address A and any deposit amount v where v > 0 and v != MinDeposit, calling Deposit with value v does not make balances(A) diverge between the reference and mutant due to the >= vs > change; specifically, the reference accepts deposits of value == MinDeposit whereas the mutant rejects them, so the distinguishing rule is: if a caller sends exactly MinDeposit, the reference increments balances(caller) by MinDeposit (and returns ok=true), while the mutant rejects that call (ok=false) — the test fuzzes caller and amount and checks that calling Deposit with value equal to the contract's MinDeposit succeeds on the reference (ok == true).

For every caller address, calling Deposit with value strictly equal to the contract's MinDeposit is accepted by the reference (Deposit executes and increments balances), whereas the mutant that uses '>' rejects that exact-MinDeposit deposit, causing behavior divergence.

For any caller address and any ether amount equal to the contract's MinDeposit, the reference C accepts the Deposit (call returns successfully) while the mutant using '>' rejects a deposit equal to MinDeposit (call reverts/fails), so the property: calling Deposit with value == MinDeposit must succeed on the reference.

Reference contract C never increases any account balance when Deposit is called with msg.value == 0 (i.e., balances[k] remains unchanged for all k), whereas the mutant that accepts zero-value deposits can increase balances (it will record a Deposit of 0 and leave balances possibly changed for some key), so the invariant 'no balance change for zero-value Deposit' holds for reference but is violated by the mutant for some inputs.

For any caller and any target key, calling Deposit with msg.value == 0 never changes any stored balances in the correct contract, but the mutant that removes the MinDeposit check can record a Deposit of 0 and thus can change balances for some inputs.

For any sender S and any amount A, if S calls Deposit with A > 0 then C.balances(S) increases by exactly A (i.e., Deposit only records nonzero deposits), whereas the mutant that removes the MinDeposit check can accept A == 0 and still push a History entry leaving balances unchanged for S but can cause balances of other addresses to change only if a malicious Log contract misbehaves; instead, we target that Deposit with any A never changes balances of addresses != caller (only caller's balance may increase) — the reference preserves that balances for any other key K != caller remain unchanged, but the mutant can break this when Log.AddMessage externally re-enters and manipulates storage (we deploy a malicious Log that re-enters and causes another account's balance to be modified); therefore the invariant: Deposit never changes balances of any address other than msg.sender.

Depositing through Deposit() never increases any other account's balances (only msg.sender's balance may increase); removing the MinDeposit check allows a malicious Log contract to re-enter on a zero-value or small deposit and cause balances of some other address to increase, so the mutant can violate the invariant that all balances[k] for k != caller remain unchanged after Deposit.

For any caller and any deposit amount >= MinDeposit, calling Deposit increases that caller's balances by the sent amount; the mutant inverted the conditional so valid large deposits are rejected and thus this property can be violated.

For any caller and any deposit amount, if Deposit is called with msg.value < MinDeposit then balances[msg.sender] must not change (reference keeps small deposits ignored); the mutant inverts the check so small deposits are accepted and thus can change balances for some inputs.

For every caller and sent amount >= MinDeposit, calling Deposit either (in the correct contract) increases that caller's balances by exactly the sent amount (i.e. balances(caller) after = before + value); the mutant inverts the conditional and thus for some caller/amount >= MinDeposit the balance will not increase, violating this rule.

For any caller and any deposit value, calling Deposit with msg.value < MinDeposit does not change the contract's total recorded balance for that caller (i.e., balances(caller) remains the same); the mutant inverted the conditional and will accept small deposits, causing balances(caller) to increase for some fuzzed inputs.

For every caller and deposit amount >= MinDeposit, the reference contract records the deposit by increasing balances(caller) by that amount; the mutant inverts the check and will, for some caller/amount >= MinDeposit, fail to increase balances, violating this rule.

For any caller and deposit amount >= MinDeposit, the reference contract never makes any account's balances decrease after Deposit (balances[k] post-call >= balances[k] pre-call for all k); the mutant without the overflow check can overflow and make some account's balance wrap to a smaller value, violating this rule.

For any caller and deposit amount, calling Deposit never decreases any account's stored balance (every balances[k] after Deposit is >= before); removing the overflow check allows balances to wrap and become smaller for some key, violating this.

For any depositor and any deposit amount >= MinDeposit, executing Deposit never decreases the stored balances[address] for any address (i.e. every balances[key] after the call is >= before); the mutant removes the overflow check so a large deposit can overflow and make some balances[key] wrap to a smaller value, violating this.

For any caller and any deposit amount >= MinDeposit, executing Deposit never decreases any account's stored balances[key] (balances[key]_after >= balances[key]_before for all keys); removing the overflow check allows an overflow wrap so some key's balance can become smaller, violating this.

For any depositor and any deposit amount >= MinDeposit, if the depositor's own balance plus the deposit does not overflow (i.e., balances[depositor] + amount >= balances[depositor]) then after Deposit the depositor's recorded balance equals the prior balance plus amount; the mutant removes the overflow guard so there exist inputs that violate this invariant.

For any caller and deposit amount >= MinDeposit, the reference contract always increments the caller's balances by the deposited amount before any external log is visible, so reading balances(caller) immediately after Deposit returns yields previous + amount; the mutant that logs before updating can cause the publicly visible balances mapping to differ (for some key) after Deposit completes (because an external reverter or reentrant callee may affect ordering), so the mutant breaks the rule.

After any Deposit call that sends >= MinDeposit from a depositor EOA, the reference increments balances(depositor) by the amount (so balances(depositor) == prior + amount); the mutant that logs before updating can be broken by a reentrant attacker that re-enters during the external log call, causing balances for some key to differ after Deposit.

Invariant: For any depositor and deposit amount >= MinDeposit, after Deposit returns the reference contract's balances(depositor) equals its prior value plus the amount; the mutant that logs before updating can be broken when the log call re-enters or otherwise triggers actions that observe the mapping during the external call, causing balances for some key to differ after Deposit.

For any depositor and amount >= MinDeposit, after Deposit returns the contract's balances for any address (queried via the public getter) is unchanged by external reentrancy triggered during logging in the reference; the mutant that logs before updating allows a reentrant attacker to observe and alter balances so some address's balance can differ after Deposit.

For any depositor and any deposit amount >= MinDeposit, the reference contract ensures that after Deposit returns the depositor's balances equals its prior value plus the deposit amount (i.e., balances depositor is updated atomically before any external effects); the mutant that logs before updating allows a reentrant attacker triggered by the logging call to change balances so this equality can be violated.

Reference C: calling Deposit() with msg.value == 0 never changes any stored balances (balances[k] remains equal to its previous value for all k); mutant M inserts require(msg.value>0) causing zero-value calls to revert and therefore can produce a differing observed behavior (revert vs no-op) for some inputs.

For every caller and observed key, calling Deposit with msg.value == 0 is a no-op on the reference (balances[k] unchanged and call does not revert); the mutant adds require(msg.value>0) so a zero-value Deposit reverts, breaking the no-op property for some inputs.

Invariant: when a caller successfully deposits >= MinDeposit, the most-recent log entry recorded by the contract's Log (History.last) must reflect the deposit event with the same msg.value and sender and must appear after the caller's balance has been increased; the mutant that logs before updating balances can produce a History entry whose recorded Val/Sender are correct but which would be observable (by comparing balances and log sequence) as occurring before the balance change, breaking the rule that any visible Deposit log corresponds to the post-deposit balance (i.e., History last Val equals amount and address(c).balance increased by that amount and balances[caller] >= previous balance + amount).

For any caller and deposit amount >= MinDeposit that results in a successful Deposit call, the contract's recorded caller balance (balances[caller]) must be at least previous_balance + amount and the contract's Ether balance must increase by exactly amount; the mutant that logs before updating balances can still transfer Ether but may produce logs observable before the state change — however the core distinguishing fact is that after Deposit completes, balances[caller] must reflect the added amount and address(c).balance increased by amount, which the mutant can violate for some reentrant adversary that re-enters between log and state update.

For every caller and deposit amount >= MinDeposit, after Deposit returns successfully the caller's recorded balance (balances[caller]) equals its previous balance plus msg.value and the contract's Ether balance increased by msg.value; the mutant that logs before updating balances can be exploited by a reentrant attacker to make the log occur before the balance update and disrupt this postcondition.

For any caller and deposit amount >= MinDeposit where Deposit returns successfully, the contract's recorded balances[caller] after the call equals its previous balance plus msg.value; the mutant (which emits the external log before updating balances) can be reentrancy-exploited to make Deposit return successfully while balances[caller] does not reflect the added amount.

For any caller and deposit amount >= MinDeposit, if a Deposit call returns successfully then the caller's recorded balances[caller] must equal previous_balance + amount (i.e. Deposit always updates balances before any external call can observe the pre-update state); the mutant that logs (external call) before updating balances can be reentrancy-exploited to make Deposit return while balances[caller] did not increase, violating this rule.

After any Deposit() call that sends at least MinDeposit, the contract's balances[msg.sender] increases by exactly the sent amount (i.e., new balance == old balance + msg.value); the mutant that overwrites balance with msg.value breaks this for callers who already had a nonzero balance.

For any caller and any deposit amount >= MinDeposit, calling Deposit increases the caller's stored balance by exactly the deposited amount (new balance == old balance + msg.value); the mutant that overwrites the balance with msg.value breaks this when the caller had a pre-existing nonzero balance.

For any caller and any deposit amount >= MinDeposit, after calling Deposit the caller's stored balance equals the previous balance plus msg.value; the mutant that sets balances[msg.sender] = msg.value (overwriting) violates this when the caller already has a nonzero balance.

For any two sequential deposits by the same externally owned account where both deposits are >= MinDeposit, the reference contract's stored balance after the second deposit equals the sum of the two deposits (i.e., deposits are cumulative); the mutant that overwrites balance with the last msg.value breaks this when the first deposit is nonzero and the second deposit also >= MinDeposit.

For any externally owned caller and any deposit amount >= MinDeposit, if the caller's prior balance is zero then after Deposit the stored balance equals msg.value; the mutant that overwrites with msg.value still satisfies this when prior balance is zero, so to distinguish we instead require that for any two different callers who each deposit >= MinDeposit, their balances are independent (one caller's second deposit does not alter the other caller's balance) — the mutant breaks independence when the same caller is reused incorrectly (we fuzz two distinct addresses and two amounts to catch overwriting behavior when the same address is mistakenly used).

For any caller and any attached value >= MinDeposit, calling Deposit increases the caller's recorded balance by that value (and thus c.balances(caller) - prior == value); the mutant inverts the condition and only records deposits when msg.value < MinDeposit, breaking this rule for values >= MinDeposit.

For any caller and any deposit amount >= MinDeposit, the reference contract records the deposit by increasing balances(caller) by that amount; the mutant inverts the check and fails to record such deposits for amounts >= MinDeposit.

For any caller and any deposit amount, if msg.value >= MinDeposit then after Deposit() the caller's recorded balance increases by msg.value; the mutant inverts the condition and fails to record such deposits for amounts >= MinDeposit.

For every caller and any deposit amount less than MinDeposit, neither contract records the deposit (balances unchanged); the mutant incorrectly records only deposits when msg.value < MinDeposit while the reference records only when msg.value >= MinDeposit — therefore the invariant: if msg.value < MinDeposit then balances(caller) does NOT increase holds for the reference for all admissible inputs and is violated by the mutant for some inputs.

For any caller and any deposit amount x, if x >= MinDeposit then after Deposit() the caller's recorded balance increases by x; the mutant inverts the check and therefore there exist x >= MinDeposit where the mutant does not increase the balance (violating the rule).

After a successful CashOut call the contract's recorded balance for the caller is decreased by the withdrawn amount (i.e., balances[caller] is reduced by _am); the mutant that performs the external transfer before decrement can be exploited by a reentrant attacker to end up with a larger recorded balance than it should (breaking this invariant).

For every caller and withdraw amount, if CashOut returns (does not revert) then the caller's recorded balance in C is decreased by exactly the withdrawn amount (balances[caller] after successful CashOut == balances_before - _am); the mutant that sends funds before updating the balance allows a reentrant caller to withdraw but keep its on-chain balance larger, violating this invariant.

For any caller and withdraw amount where CashOut succeeds, the caller's recorded balance in C is decreased by exactly the withdrawn amount; the mutant that transfers funds before decrementing allows a reentrant malicious callee to withdraw extra funds and preserve or increase its recorded balance, violating this rule.

For any caller and amount where CashOut returns successfully, the contract's recorded balance for that caller decreases (address(c).balance changes accordingly and balances[caller] is decreased by the withdrawn amount) — the mutant that transfers funds before decrementing allows a reentrant attacker to make the external call reenter and cause the recorded balance not to decrease, violating this invariant.

For any caller and withdrawal amount where CashOut is invoked, if the external call to send funds reverts then the contract's recorded balance for that caller must remain unchanged (the reference reverts the whole operation), whereas the mutant that performs the external call before decrement may reduce the balance even when the external transfer fails or is reverted by a malicious counterparty, causing balances to diverge.

For any caller and any withdraw amount <= their recorded balance, a successful CashOut call reduces that caller's stored balances[msg.sender] by exactly the withdrawn amount; the mutant that omits the subtraction leaves the stored balance unchanged and thus violates this invariant for some inputs.

For any caller and any withdrawal amount <= their recorded balance, after a successful CashOut the caller's stored balance decreases by exactly the withdrawn amount; the mutant that omits the subtraction leaves the stored balance unchanged, so for some inputs the post-call stored balance will not have decreased and the property is violated.

For any depositor and any withdrawal amount that is <= their recorded balance and where the low-level transfer to the recipient succeeds, the contract's public balances(depositor) must strictly decrease after CashOut; the mutant that omits subtracting the amount can leave balances unchanged when the transfer succeeds.
